title: Lock types, mechanisms and security-grade selection
audience: Workers who select and fit locks under a licensed or confirmed scope
learningOutcomes: Identify the main lock types and mechanisms and their typical use in residential doors.
Select a lock grade that matches the door, the frame and the risk, using the manufacturer data.
Identify when a lock must be referred because it is a fire door, an access system or a master-keyed installation.

instruction.heading: Lock types and what each one does
instruction.body:
A residential door usually has two kinds of lock working together. A latch is a spring-loaded bolt that holds the door closed when it is pulled shut, and it releases when the handle is pressed. It gives convenience, but it does little to resist force. A deadlock, which is also called a deadbolt, is a solid bolt that is thrown by a key or a turn-knob. It holds the door against pressure and is the part that resists a forced entry. Many doors combine a latch in the handle set with a separate deadlock, and the two should be considered together.

The mechanism is only one part of the lock. A cylinder is the keyed part that operates the bolt. Cylinders differ in their keying system, the number and type of pins or other components inside, and their resistance to picking and drilling. Lock bodies are fitted into the door in different ways. A mortice lock sits in a pocket cut into the edge of the door. A rim lock is surface-mounted. A cylinder-only lock is a cylinder that works with a separate bolt in the same door.

A lock mechanism, its cylinder, the strike plate and the door frame all share the load of a forced entry. A strong cylinder in a weak frame does not give a secure door, because the force travels into the frame, and the strike plate and its fixings are where the door gives way. Check the whole assembly, not one component alone.

instruction.heading: Measuring, specifying and selecting by grade
instruction.body: Select a lock grade that the manufacturer rates for the door, the frame and the risk. The grade ratings and the test standards are set out in the manufacturer's data. Record the model, the grade rating as stated, and the manufacturer data reference. Before you fit anything, measure the door and check the lock specification. Measure the door thickness. Measure the backset, which is the distance from the edge of the door to the centre of the lock spindle or bore. Many residential locks are listed for a particular backset, and for example a lock may be listed for a 60 mm or a 70 mm backset; the lock you have must match the measurement you take, and the example values are not a rule for any product. Check the cylinder length against the door thickness and the lock specification. A cylinder that is too long can protrude or foul the mechanism, and one that is too short may not engage properly. Check the frame and the strike plate. The strike plate and its fixings must reach solid timber or a fixing rated for the frame material. Screws into soft or split timber, or into a frame that is loose in the wall, do not give the grade the lock is rated for. Where a frame is weak, recommend remediation and quote it separately rather than fitting a high-grade cylinder that the frame cannot support. Where the door is a fire door, the lock and its hardware are part of the fire-resistance system. Refer the work as set out in “Door installation: frame, hinge and fire-door boundary”, and do not treat a fire door as an ordinary door for lock selection.

instruction.heading: Keys, master keying and access systems
instruction.body: Some lock jobs are more than a single lock. A master-keyed system uses several cylinders that open with a common key, and the key plan decides who can open which door. An access system uses cards, codes or electronic readers to control entry. Both need a documented key plan or access design, a record of who holds each key or credential, and an agreed process for lost keys and changes. Refer these installations rather than fitting them as standard hardware, unless the scope and the licence position for that work are confirmed for the job. Record the key numbers and the people issued with them, and check the licence position before any work begins.

procedure: Record the door type, thickness, backset, cylinder length, frame material and the risk for the location.
Choose a lock and cylinder rated for the risk, using the manufacturer data for the model.
Check the lock specification against the measured door before drilling or cutting.
Check the frame and strike plate, and confirm the fixings reach solid material or a fixing rated for the frame.
Refer any fire door, access system or master-keyed installation rather than fitting it as standard.
Record the lock model, the grade as stated, the manufacturer data reference, the keys issued and the fitting date.

workedExamples.situation: A client wants a high-grade cylinder fitted to a hollow-core door in a weak timber frame. The strike plate sits in a frame that moves when pushed.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the cylinder be fitted as requested?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not without addressing the frame. A high-grade cylinder in a weak frame does not secure the door, because the frame and strike plate carry the load of a forced entry. Record the movement in the frame and the condition of the strike fixings, and photograph them with permission. Recommend a frame and strike check and remediation, and quote that work separately. Confirm the licence position for the work before fitting the lock, as set out in the safety notes below.

workedExamples.situation: A strata manager asks for a master-keyed set of six cylinders for a residential block, with the key plan to be decided later.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you agree to do now?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not fit the set as standard hardware. A master-keyed installation needs a key plan, a record of who holds each key and a process for lost keys before fitting. Record the request, the number of cylinders and the decision maker. Refer the job, and confirm the licence position for the installation in the relevant state or territory before accepting it.

workedExamples.situation: A replacement lock is needed for a rental door that is not part of any building work. The tenant wants the lock swapped this afternoon.
workedExamples.reasoning: In Queensland the building-work exemption covers installing basic security items while a building is being constructed, repaired or renovated. Removing and refitting a household lock on a building that is not undergoing that work needs a security equipment installer licence, and the exemption does not cover it. Confirm whether building work is under way before you accept the job, and record the position.

equipmentAndPpe: Manufacturer data sheet for each lock and cylinder, with the model and grade as stated.
Measuring tape, backset gauge and door thickness measure.
Spirit level and straight edge for checking the door and frame.
Drill and bits matched to the fixings and the frame material.
Eye protection, and hearing protection where the task risk assessment calls for it.
Dust mask for cutting timber or masonry.

commonErrors.error: Fitting a high-grade cylinder in a weak frame.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the frame and strike plate, and recommend remediation where they cannot take the fixings.

commonErrors.error: Using the wrong backset or cylinder length.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure the door and the backset, and check the lock specification before drilling.

commonErrors.error: Fitting a fire door's lock as standard hardware.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer fire doors and their hardware, as set out in “Door installation: frame, hinge and fire-door boundary”.

commonErrors.error: Fitting a master-keyed or access system without a key plan.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the installation until the key plan, the key register and the licence position are confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the building-work exemption covers a household lock swap.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm whether building work is under way, and check the licence position for the job before accepting it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Queensland: a security equipment installer licence authorises work on locks for commercial or residential areas, and the licensing page states that in most cases a licence is needed to be a locksmith. Retail key cutting does not require the licence. Installing basic security items in a building during its construction, repair or renovation is an exemption. The exemption does not extend to repairing, servicing, maintaining or replacing basic security items when no construction, repair or renovation is under way. Basic security items include household locks, even if they are damaged (Queensland Government, security equipment installer licence page; last updated 21 October 2026).

The Security Providers Act 1993 (Qld), in the in-force version dated 5 December 2024, defines a basic security item in section 6B(3). The definition includes an electronic or mechanical lock used for basic household security, with a door lock, window lock or padlock given as examples. Section 6B(2)(e) states that a person is not a security equipment installer merely because they install a basic security item in a building that someone else owns or occupies, while that building is being constructed, repaired or renovated.

Fire doors: the Queensland Fire Department information sheet (version 09/2025) states that hardware including closers, handles, locks and vision panels is part of a fire door's fire-resistance rating, and that the hardware must be tested and approved by a registered testing authority. The sheet also states that only a suitably licensed person can certify, inspect or test a fire door, and it describes locksmith work on components including locks as not needing a licence. This course does not rely on that statement for fire-door work, and refers fire doors to a competent specialist.
Victoria: the Victoria Police private security page (updated 2 November 2026) refers to private security licence activities but does not name locksmith work.
Completing this lesson does not give a locksmith licence or authority to fit, alter or certify fire-rated doors, and it does not authorise master-keyed or access-system installation.

qualityStandard: The lock grade is matched to the door, the frame and the risk, using the manufacturer data for the model.
The backset, door thickness and cylinder length are measured and checked against the lock specification before fitting.
The frame and strike fixings are checked before the lock is relied on, and any weakness is recorded and quoted separately.
Fire doors, access systems and master-keyed installations are referred.
documentationEvidence: Lock selection record with the model, the grade as stated and the manufacturer data reference.
Measurement record with the door thickness, backset and cylinder length.
Frame and strike check record, with photographs taken with permission where a weakness is found.
Referral note for any fire door, access system or master-keyed installation, and the key register where keys are issued.
summary: A strong lock in a weak frame does not secure the door.
Select by the manufacturer grade for the model, the measured door and the frame condition.
Refer fire doors, access systems and master-keyed work, and confirm the licence position before any job is accepted.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants a high-grade cylinder fitted to a weak timber frame. What is correct?
options: Fit it as requested, because the cylinder is rated high for security
Fit a cheaper cylinder instead, since it will still be strong enough for the job
Check the frame and strike, recommend remediation, and quote it separately
Remove the frame so the cylinder fits, since the frame is the main problem here

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen before fitting a lock to a fire door?
options: Fit the lock as standard hardware on the day
Remove the fire-rating marking from the door
Fit a lock taken from another door on the site
Refer the fire door to a competent specialist

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must the backset be measured before a lock is chosen?
options: It shows the colour of the door and its finish, which the owner chose
The lock must match the measured backset, or it will not fit the door as specified
It decides the price of the cylinder and the labour needed for the whole job today
It is only needed for rim locks and not for mortise locks, so it can be skipped
